title: SuperTuxKart 1.5 uncapped Vulkan Mailbox: the panel reading Android's screen from shared memory, the in-band path and BlueStacks 5 Pie64, alternated in one session

workload.measurement_source: frame count and profiled duration of the game's own frame report

power_mode.name: Best performance
power_mode.note: Every step recorded this overlay as the one before it, the active one and the one put back: the mode was already on before the session and stayed on through it. Balanced was not measured.

client_build.branch: feature/display-shared-memory, started from 6ac2918 (the v0.24.0 source, before the Linux-only change of v0.24.1)
client_build.what_it_contains: the first two feature commits of v0.25.0; src/display.rs, src/display/ and src/ui.rs at that commit are identical to the release branch at its second feature commit (Keep the shared memory panel live and fall back when the engine writes elsewhere)
client_build.what_it_lacks: the feature commits made after it, the v0.24.1 change and the version number 0.25.0
client_build.evidence_in_the_receipts: the SHA-256 of the executable only; no receipt ties that hash to a commit or records the version the executable reports

rustemudroid.started_by: a lab harness; the harness set the engine environment and the transport variable, and the client's own performance engine setting was not used

lab_profile_config_ini_keys.note: Read from the lab profile's config.ini after the session; that file was last written on 2026-11-26 at 15:29. Android reported gltransport=asg in every step. The guest's kernel command line was not read back in this series.

engine.note: The step receipts name the stage folder. The hashes are those of its staging record of 2026-11-26, the same three as in the series of that day; the binaries were not hashed again during this session.

comparison.reading: RustEmuDroid was ahead in this session, and shared memory was faster than the in-band path in the same session. BlueStacks measured about 14% less than on 2026-11-26 on the same PC and workload, cause unknown, so this series does not establish a lead over BlueStacks.

not_measured: the feature commits of v0.25.0 made after the timed build
shared memory with any engine other than this performance engine build
the settings applied by the client's own performance engine preset
shared memory with Fit video frames to the window off (full 1600x900 frames)
an in-band arm at the default panel size
the stock engine that first-time setup installs
not_established: why BlueStacks measured about 14% less than on 2026-11-26
the commit and the version of the client executable, beyond its SHA-256 (the commit comes from the lab notes)
the Windows power plan (only the overlay was recorded)
whether the kernel parameters reached the guest's command line (they are in the lab profile's config.ini)
